beats.text: Rooftop off Bourdillon Road. She's early. There's a printed agenda beside your plate. Item 4: 'Intentions.'
Chidinma will take minutes. Ignore her. Shall we begin? Item 1: why are you three minutes late?
{tell}

engaged.text: Her clutch falls open. A velvet ring box. She snaps it shut. Her fingers are bare.

collapsing.text: Her phone lights up face-up: 'Ma, salary?' Then the same from three other numbers.

tired.text: Item 2 is 'Salary'. She asks your exact take-home. Chidinma writes. Adaeze doesn't.

choices.label: Play along. Answer every item like a job interview.
choices.receipt: You answered her agenda like a job interview.

outcomes.text: You score 7.5 out of 10. Chidinma underlines 'punctual (eventually)'.

tired.text: 'Finally, a straight answer.' She smiles for the first time. Chidinma types 'SMILED' in capitals.

choices.label: Inflate your salary. Small small. It's Ikoyi.
choices.receipt: You inflated your salary on the first date.

outcomes.text: 'Impressive.' Chidinma writes the number down. In pen.

tired.text: She hears the lie before you finish it. 'Please don't perform for me. I've had enough performers.'

collapsing.text: Her eyes light up a little too much. 'Interesting. Very, very interesting.' She orders more wine.

choices.label: Slide over your own agenda. Item 1: who's paying?
choices.receipt: You brought your own agenda to the date.

outcomes.text: She laughs so hard the waiter reverses. 'Motion noted. I'm paying. Item 2.'
Minutes: 'Candidate raised payment before starters.' She reads it back to you. Slowly.

choices.label: 'No minutes. This is a date, not an AGM.'
choices.receipt: You asked her to stop the minutes.

outcomes.text: She stares. Then sends Chidinma home in an Uber. The date gets slower, and better.

tired.text: 'Nobody has ever said no to me at dinner.' She sends Chidinma home and slips her heels off under the table.

choices.label: [Corporate] 'Send the minutes as PDF. Track changes on.'
choices.receipt: You asked for the minutes with track changes.

outcomes.text: Chidinma stops typing. Adaeze laughs into her napkin. 'You read emails. Marry me. Joking. Item 5.'

choices.label: [Sugar] 'Item 5: my transport. Let's table it now.'
choices.receipt: You tabled your transport money on the agenda.

outcomes.text: She transfers ₦30k. Reference: 'TRANSPORT (AGENDA ITEM 5)'. Chidinma attaches the receipt.
'I don't fund. I invest.' Minutes: 'Candidate is a cost centre.'

beats.text: A white Range Rover stops at your Ojuelegba bus stop. Danfo conductors stop shouting to look. The doors stay locked.
Before you get in: surname, state of origin, and your father's profession. In that order.
{tell}

engaged.text: 'My uncle says the families are close,' she adds. Which families? You haven't mentioned yours.

collapsing.text: On the windscreen, a sticker you weren't meant to read: 'ASSET FINANCE. DO NOT REMOVE.'

tired.text: Her phone rings: 'Mummy'. She declines it. 'Don't take it personally. I'm hiding you on purpose.'

choices.label: Tell the truth. Your dad sells phones at Computer Village.
choices.receipt: You told her your father sells phones at Computer Village.

outcomes.text: She nods slowly. 'Commerce. Good.' The locks click open.

tired.text: She unlocks before you finish. 'A trader's child. Thank God. You know the price of things.'

engaged.text: The locks click. Then she texts someone: 'Surname fine. Village not confirmed.' She sees you see it.

choices.label: Invent a chieftaincy title. 'Ichie' sounds correct.
choices.receipt: You invented a chieftaincy title on day one.

outcomes.text: The locks open like a palace gate. 'Ichie. Uncle will be pleased.' Uncle will also check.

tired.text: 'Ichie of where?' She looks exhausted. 'Every person I meet is a chief. I wanted a person.' She opens the door anyway.

choices.label: 'Ask me inside. The AC is the first agenda item.'
choices.receipt: You told her to ask you inside the car.

outcomes.text: She laughs once. Unlocks. 'Fair. Lagos heat is not a negotiation.'

choices.label: [Runs] 'My people are from everywhere.' Smile.
choices.receipt: You told her your people are from everywhere.

outcomes.text: 'Interesting CV.' She opens the door. She's smiling at the windscreen, not at you. Progress.
'Everywhere is nowhere.' She drives one full lap of the roundabout before letting you in.

choices.label: [Big Boy] Point across the road: 'Mine's the G-Wagon.'
choices.receipt: You flexed your G-Wagon at her Range Rover.

outcomes.text: She looks at it. Then at you. 'Leased?' It is. You both laugh. She unlocks.

tired.text: 'Another one.' She drives off. Then reverses. 'Get in. Leave the car. Be a person tonight.'

beats.text: Her flagship boutique on Admiralty Way. Mirrors, mannequins, a security man who salutes. She hands you a garment bag.
Change into this. My people don't date in polo. Then we'll talk.
{tell}

engaged.text: Behind the till, a desk calendar: 'SAT 14. INTRODUCTION. ENUGU.' Circled twice, in red.

collapsing.text: Every rack has a red tag: 70% OFF. Even the security man is wearing one.

tired.text: Her phone: 'Gala tonight 8pm, Madam?' She types 'Cancel. Something came up.' You are the something.

choices.label: Wear it. It fits suspiciously well.
choices.receipt: You wore the outfit she picked for you.

outcomes.text: She walks around you twice. 'Now you look like a decision.'

collapsing.text: It fits. The tag says ₦380k, slashed to ₦114k. 'Keep it,' she says, a bit too quickly.

choices.label: 'I came as myself. Take it or leave it.'
choices.receipt: You refused her outfit and stayed in your polo.

outcomes.text: She sighs. 'Fine. But we're eating somewhere dark.'

tired.text: She stares. Then laughs. 'Nobody ever says no to the bag.' She hangs it back up herself.

choices.label: Insist on paying for it. ₦120k. Pride.
choices.broke_text: Your account said 'buy polo, it's cheaper'.
choices.receipt: You insisted on paying for the outfit.

outcomes.text: She lets you. Chidinma texts her: 'Candidate pays.' Uncle will hear by dinner.

collapsing.text: She takes your card fast. The POS prints 'ACCOUNT UNDER REVIEW', then approves. She exhales like she's been underwater.

tired.text: She refunds you in front of you. 'You don't buy things from me. That's the rule.' Then she kisses your cheek.

choices.label: Offer to iron it yourself. Free labour.
choices.receipt: You offered to iron the outfit yourself.

outcomes.text: 'You're unserious.' She's grinning. 'I like unserious. In small doses.'

choices.label: [Runs] Ask for staff discount. You're basically staff.
choices.receipt: You asked for staff discount on day one.

outcomes.text: 'Fine. 100% discount. Your salary is also 0%.' She throws in a tie.
The security man escorts you to the changing room. Then, gently, out.

beats.text: Her Lekki flat, 10pm. Mid-kiss, her phone: 'Uncle'. She takes it on the balcony, in Igbo, door shut. Forty minutes.
Family business. Don't wait up. Actually, wait up.
{tell}

engaged.text: Her handbag is open on the sofa. A velvet ring box. She has never worn a ring around you.

collapsing.text: Her laptop pings on the sofa: 'Ma, salary? It's the third month.' Fourteen unread.

tired.text: Through the glass: 'No, Uncle. You will not meet this one. Not until I'm sure you'll be kind.'

choices.label: Open the bag. Just one look.
choices.receipt: You went through her handbag.

outcomes.text: Lipstick, a power bank, eleven receipts. You feel like a thief who stole nothing.

engaged.text: A solitaire. Engraved inside: 'A & E. 14.06.' You are not E.
The balcony door slides open. She sees your hand in her bag. The rain is very loud.

collapsing.text: Folded letters: 'NOTICE OF DEFAULT.' Three banks. One landlord. One very angry fabric supplier.
The balcony door slides open. She sees your hand in her bag. The rain is very loud.

tired.text: A notebook. Page one: 'Things I like about this one.' Your name, underlined twice. You put it back, ashamed.
She catches you. She doesn't shout. She just looks tired.

choices.label: Wait up. Like she said.
choices.receipt: You waited up and didn't ask about the call.

outcomes.text: She comes back at eleven and kisses you like an apology for something she won't name.

choices.label: 'Who's Uncle, and why is he forty minutes?'
choices.receipt: You asked her about the forty-minute call.

outcomes.text: 'Family.' One word. She sits closer, which is an answer and also isn't.

engaged.text: 'Uncle Obiora manages... family plans.' She changes the subject to your shoes. Your shoes are fine.

collapsing.text: 'He's my guarantor.' She hears herself. 'For the boutique. It's nothing. It's handled.'

tired.text: 'He thinks I should marry a bank. I think I should eat amala with you.' She means both sentences.

choices.label: Leave. She can call when she's done.
choices.receipt: You left while she was on the call.

outcomes.text: You're in a keke at the Phase 1 gate when she texts: 'That was rude. Also fair.'

choices.label: Order amala from Ojuelegba. She'll be hungry.
choices.receipt: You ordered her secret amala while she was on the call.

outcomes.text: She comes back to amala on the coffee table. Stops in the doorway. 'You remembered.' She eats with her hands.

choices.label: [Lover] Make pepper soup while you wait.
choices.receipt: You made her pepper soup during her call.

outcomes.text: She comes back to pepper soup. Stops in the doorway. 'Who taught you to do this?' Your mother. Thank her.

beats.text: 7:02am, an email. Subject: 'Q1 Relationship Review (CONFIDENTIAL).' From: Chidinma, PA to Adaeze.
Strengths: punctual-ish. Development areas: shoes, your 'lol'. Rating: Meets Expectations. Kindly sign and return.
{tell}

engaged.text: Attached by mistake: a calendar invite. 'Introduction ceremony, Enugu. Attendees: Adaeze, Ebuka N., both families.'

collapsing.text: CC'd by accident: a thread titled 'Ma, salary?' with 23 replies.

tired.text: Section 3, in her own handwriting: 'Salary: modest. Notes: GOOD. DO NOT LET UNCLE SEE.'

choices.label: Sign and return. Meets Expectations is a pass.
choices.receipt: You signed your own relationship review.

outcomes.text: Chidinma: 'Received with thanks.' Adaeze sends a heart, which in her company is a promotion.

choices.label: Reply with your own review of her.
choices.receipt: You sent her a performance review back.

outcomes.text: She replies at 7:40: 'Development area: humility. Fair.' Then a voice note of her laughing.
You hit reply-all. Her uncle, her banker and her pastor now know her 'listening score'.

choices.label: Call her: 'What's this attachment?'
choices.receipt: You called her about the attachment.

outcomes.text: 'Admin error.' Pause. 'Chidinma will be spoken to.'

engaged.text: 'It's a family event. Everybody's introduction. Not mine. Mostly.' Mostly.

collapsing.text: 'What thread?' Silence. 'Don't read things that aren't for you.' She hangs up first.

tired.text: 'Oh God. Section 3.' She laughs till she coughs. 'Yes. Modest is the point. Don't you dare change.'

choices.label: Leave it on read. Let HR chase you.
choices.receipt: You left her PA's review on read.

outcomes.text: Chidinma follows up at 9am, 11am and 2pm. 'Gentle reminder.' Then 'Firm reminder.'

choices.label: 'You don't have to run us like your father ran yours.'
choices.receipt: You told her she doesn't have to run you like her father did.

outcomes.text: No reply for an hour. Then: 'Chidinma, cancel the reviews. All of them.' Then, to you: 'Thank you.'

tired.text: She calls. She's crying a bit. 'Nobody's ever said it.' Chidinma is quietly reassigned to inventory.

choices.label: [Corporate] Return it with tracked changes. Upgrade yourself.
choices.receipt: You tracked-changed your own review to 'Exceeds'.

outcomes.text: Chidinma escalates. Adaeze approves every change. You are now 'Exceeds Expectations'. She's in love with your formatting.

beats.text: A man in a brown suit is waiting at your bus stop in Yaba. He has a clipboard and your secondary school photo.
Family due diligence. Twelve questions. You may decline. It will be noted.
{tell}

engaged.text: His letterhead: 'Retained by Obiora & Co., on behalf of the families.' Families. Plural.

collapsing.text: He came in her Range Rover. On the back glass: 'ASSET FINANCE. REPOSSESSION HOTLINE.'

tired.text: Question 12 is handwritten, in her writing: 'Are they kind to waiters?'

choices.label: Answer all twelve. Nothing to hide.
choices.receipt: You answered the family investigator's twelve questions.

outcomes.text: Lawal shakes your hand. 'Clean. Boring. Recommended.'

engaged.text: Lawal closes the clipboard. 'Clean. Pity.' You ask what that means. He's already in the car.

tired.text: That night: 'Lawal says you bought him Fanta. I'm sorry I sent him. I needed to know before I let myself like you.'

choices.label: 'Tell her to ask me herself.'
choices.receipt: You refused the investigator and told her to ask you herself.

outcomes.text: He writes 'UNCOOPERATIVE' in capitals. That night she calls you herself. Progress, apparently.

tired.text: She calls in ten minutes. 'You're right. That was my uncle's method. I'm sorry. Ask me anything back.'

choices.label: Slip him ₦20k: 'Write something nice.'
choices.receipt: You bribed the family investigator.

outcomes.text: He writes 'Excellent family. Very tall.' You are not tall.
He pockets it and writes 'Attempted bribery (₦20k).' Underlined. Twice.

choices.label: Put in your earphones. Board the danfo.
choices.receipt: You boarded a danfo and left the investigator standing.

outcomes.text: He chases the danfo for a full bus stop, clipboard flapping. The conductor charges him anyway.

choices.label: [Runs] Investigate him back. Who pays his fuel?
choices.receipt: You investigated the investigator.

outcomes.text: Lawal's fuel is paid by a family account. Not hers.

engaged.text: Lawal's invoice is addressed to 'The Nwosu–Obi merger committee'. Merger. With a groom.

collapsing.text: Lawal hasn't been paid in two months either. 'Join the queue,' he says.

tired.text: Lawal shows you his WhatsApp: she paid him personally, with a note: 'Be gentle. I like this one.'

beats.text: 2pm, Admiralty Way. Her boutique's shutters are half down. This morning she said she'd be 'in board meetings all day'.
Busy busy. Board. Talk tonight. xx
{tell}

engaged.text: Through the glass, a tailor is pinning her into ivory lace. Introduction-ceremony ivory.

collapsing.text: On the glass: 'EVERYTHING 70% OFF. FINAL DAYS.' A man is carrying out a mannequin 'for balance'.

tired.text: On the counter: a gala invitation, torn in half. Beside it, two amala takeaway packs. Two.

choices.label: Knock on the glass. Wave.
choices.receipt: You knocked on her boutique window.

outcomes.text: She freezes. Then lifts the shutter.

engaged.text: She steps out of the lace like it's hot. 'It's for a cousin.' The tailor says, 'Ma, your own measurements?'

collapsing.text: She lets you in. Sits on the floor between empty rails. 'Fine. You've seen it. Don't look at me like that.'

tired.text: She lifts the shutter holding the second pack. 'I was about to call you. It's amala o. Not gala.'

choices.label: Keep walking. Busy is busy.
choices.receipt: You walked past her half-shut boutique.

outcomes.text: You buy a Fanta you don't want and drink it at the bus stop, thinking.

choices.label: Take a photo. Evidence for later.
choices.receipt: You photographed her boutique through the glass.

outcomes.text: Saved. Your gallery now has a folder called 'Adaeze (Evidence)'.
Flash on. Broad daylight. She looks up, straight into your lens.

choices.label: Post it: 'Board meeting, abi? 👀'
choices.receipt: You posted her boutique's shutters online.

outcomes.text: The Parlour zooms in. Nobody knows what they're looking at, so they make things up.

collapsing.text: The Parlour zooms in on the 70% sign: 'ADA BOUTIQUE IS FINISHED.' Her suppliers screenshot it by evening.

engaged.text: Someone zooms in on the lace: 'Bride loading? 👰🏾' Her aunties like it. All of them.

choices.label: Ask Sunday Okon the security man what's happening.
choices.receipt: You asked Sunday the security man what was going on.

outcomes.text: 'Oga/Madam, I no fit talk.' Then he talks for twenty minutes.

engaged.text: 'Na fitting, for her introduction. The groom family dey come Saturday.' He looks sorry for you.

collapsing.text: 'Three months salary, nobody pay. But Madam dey try. She sell her own car last week.' He salutes the empty window.

tired.text: 'She cancel gala again. Na you she dey wait for. Go inside, abeg, the amala don cold.'

beats.text: Her flat. A pitch deck on the TV. Slide 1: 'ADA BOUTIQUE: SERIES A.' Slide 2 is a photo of you.
Minimum ticket ₦500k. Five percent of the company. Chidinma has the DocuSign ready.
{tell}

engaged.text: Slide 9, 'Strategic Partners': 'The Nwosu family (merger pending).' Her uncle's name is in the footnote.

collapsing.text: Her phone on the table: 'Ma, salary? We are at your gate.' She turns it over without looking.

tired.text: Slide 7 is just your salary, circled: 'Too small to invest. Perfect.' She clicks past it, embarrassed.

choices.receipt: You invested ₦500k in her boutique.

outcomes.text: Signed. You own five percent of something.

choices.label: Offer ₦20k. 'Angel round.'
choices.receipt: You offered her a ₦20k angel round.

outcomes.text: Chidinma logs you as 'Friends & Family, Tier 4'. Adaeze is trying not to laugh.

collapsing.text: She takes it. It goes straight to the security man's salary. He salutes you every time now.

choices.label: 'Send me the audited accounts first.'
choices.receipt: You asked for her audited accounts.

outcomes.text: She sends audited accounts. They are audited. You're impressed and slightly attracted.

engaged.text: Clean accounts. Note 14: 'Proposed marriage-linked merger, Q3.' You read Note 14 three times.

collapsing.text: The accounts arrive three days late, unaudited, watermarked DRAFT. Revenue: 'pending'.

choices.label: 'I don't mix money and love.'
choices.receipt: You told her you don't mix money and love.

outcomes.text: She closes the laptop. 'Noted.' The temperature in the flat drops two degrees.

tired.text: 'Good. Neither do I. That was a test.' She closes the laptop. 'Let's eat. You pick.'

choices.label: Confess: 'My salary isn't what I told you.'
choices.receipt: You confessed you'd inflated your salary.

outcomes.text: She blinks. 'Thank you for telling me before it cost you.' She deletes slide 2.

choices.receipt: You asked about the liquidity joke she'd made.

outcomes.text: She stops the slideshow. 'You remember everything.' It's not clear if that's good.

collapsing.text: She sits down. 'Three months of payroll. Two banks. One Range Rover I don't own.' Finally, the real deck.

tired.text: 'It was a joke, but yes, my accountant hates me.' She shows you everything. It's fine. She's just dramatic.

choices.label: [Big Boy] Counter: ₦250k for a board seat.
choices.receipt: You bought a board seat for ₦250k.

outcomes.text: Your first board meeting is dinner. Your second is breakfast. You're not complaining.

collapsing.text: You're on the board of a company in receivership. Your first meeting is with the bank.

beats.text: A WhatsApp broadcast from Chidinma: 'ASO-EBI FOR THE FAMILY EVENT. ₦180k per head. Gele not included. Pay by Friday.'
Wear it. Uncle notices who didn't.

engaged.text: The flyer: 'Introduction Ceremony. Adaeze & —' The rest is cropped. Badly. You can see an 'E'.

collapsing.text: The account number is the boutique's. Payment reference: 'SALARY ARREARS (ASO-EBI)'.

tired.text: A second text from her, private: 'Don't buy it. Don't come. I'm not ready to feed you to them.'

choices.receipt: You paid ₦180k for aso-ebi.

choices.label: 'Whose event is this, exactly?'
choices.receipt: You asked whose event the aso-ebi was for.

outcomes.text: 'Family.' Typing. Stops. Typing. 'It's complicated.'

choices.receipt: You asked her to sponsor your aso-ebi.

choices.label: Say very little. Eat two full plates.
choices.receipt: You said little and ate two plates, like she warned.

outcomes.text: Uncle watches you finish plate two. 'This one eats.' From him, that's a blessing.

choices.label: Ask Chidinma to stop typing. Like the first dinner.
choices.receipt: You asked Chidinma to stop the minutes in front of the family.

outcomes.text: Chidinma looks at Adaeze. Adaeze nods. The iPad goes dark. Uncle looks at you like a rival chairman.

choices.label: [Corporate] Present a one-page deck on yourself.
choices.receipt: You presented a one-page deck on yourself to her family.

outcomes.text: Uncle asks for a printed copy. An aunty asks if you're single. Adaeze answers for you.

beats.text: A VIP booth on Ozumba Mbadiwe. A man in white agbada sends over a bottle and a card: 'For Ada. Remember me? Ebuka.'
Ignore him. Oil money. He thinks I'm a merger.
{tell}

engaged.text: Ebuka raises his glass. On his pinky: a band engraved 'A & E'. Matching set. Hers is in her bag.

collapsing.text: Ebuka, loud: 'Ada! I hear your staff are protesting? I can help. Terms apply!'

tired.text: Her phone: 'Gala 10pm, you're the keynote.' She types 'Sick.' She has never looked healthier.

choices.label: Send the bottle back with a thank-you note.
choices.receipt: You sent the rival's bottle back with a note.

outcomes.text: Ebuka reads the note, nods, tips the waiter, leaves. Classy rival. Annoying.

choices.label: Send him a bigger bottle. ₦150k. Let him feel it.
choices.broke_text: Your account is not in this fight.
choices.receipt: You sent Ebuka a ₦150k bottle to win the booth.

outcomes.text: The VIP section goes 'OHHHH'. Ebuka salutes. You won. She's furious you made it a show.

engaged.text: Ebuka laughs. 'I like this one, Ada. Bring them to the wedding.' Wedding.

choices.label: Send him ₦2k suya 'with compliments'.
choices.receipt: You sent the rival a ₦2k suya.

outcomes.text: The suya lands on his table. The whole VIP laughs. Even Ebuka eats it.

choices.label: Walk over: 'Ebuka. What's the merger?'
choices.receipt: You asked Ebuka about the 'merger'.

outcomes.text: He smiles. 'Ask her.'

engaged.text: 'Our wedding, my friend. Introduction is the 14th. Didn't she tell you?' He seems genuinely sorry.

collapsing.text: 'I'm buying her company for the price of a Range Rover. Hers.' He winks. 'Don't worry, I'll keep the staff.'

tired.text: 'She turned me down three times. Congratulations, I suppose.' He means it. He buys you a drink.

choices.label: Pull her to the dance floor. Let him watch.
choices.receipt: You danced with her in front of the rival.

outcomes.text: Three songs. Ebuka leaves after one. She forgets he exists after two.

beats.text: You booked a table for two. She arrives with four friends, Chidinma, and a cousin 'visiting from London'.
They wanted to see you. Order anything. You're hosting, abi?
{tell}

engaged.text: One friend, loud: 'So is it gold or ivory on the 14th?' Everyone kicks her under the table.

collapsing.text: All her friends wear her boutique's dresses. One still has the 70% OFF tag on the sleeve.

tired.text: Her friends ask your salary in turns. She glares at each one. 'Stop it. That's not why.'

choices.label: Order for the whole table. ₦200k. Pride.
choices.broke_text: Your account refuses to host London.
choices.receipt: You hosted her friends for ₦200k.

outcomes.text: The friends approve loudly. The London cousin asks for your number 'for business'.

choices.label: 'Small chops for the table. Mains are split.'
choices.receipt: You bought small chops and split the mains.

outcomes.text: Puff-puff diplomacy. The friends respect a budget. Adaeze respects a spreadsheet.

choices.label: 'I booked for two. I'll wait for the two.'
choices.receipt: You told her you'd wait for the table for two.

outcomes.text: She sends the friends to the bar. They're offended. She's intrigued.

tired.text: She sends them to another table. 'Thank you. They've scared off four people this year.'

choices.label: Let them grill you. Every question. Keep smiling.
choices.receipt: You let her friends grill you for three hours.

outcomes.text: Three hours. Your exes, your rent, your mother's maiden name. You pass. You also need to lie down for a week.

tired.text: Three hours. You pass. In the car she says, 'Nobody's ever sat through all of it.' You're too tired to answer.

engaged.text: Three hours. Question 41: 'Would you attend a wedding as a guest?' Everyone goes quiet. You need to lie down.

choices.label: Win the friends over. Ignore her a little.
choices.receipt: You charmed her friends.

outcomes.text: The group chat votes. You pass, 4-1. The London cousin abstains.
One friend likes you a bit too much. She notices. Everyone notices.

choices.label: [Sugar] Ask the London cousin for transport.
choices.receipt: You asked her London cousin for transport money.

outcomes.text: £20 lands. The cousin says 'I like this one.' Adaeze pretends to be appalled.
The cousin sends the screenshot to the group. Adaeze's face says 'item 6: decorum'.

beats.text: Dinner. A man in a perfect agbada walks to your table and kisses her hand. There's a ring on it now.
Good evening. I'm Ebuka. Her fiancé. And you must be the... consultant?
{tell}

engaged.text: The ring from her bag is on her finger. She keeps turning it, like she's trying to unscrew it.

choices.label: 'Is it on paper, or in your heart?'
choices.receipt: You asked her if the engagement was paper or heart.

outcomes.text: She looks at Ebuka. Then at you. 'Paper. My uncle's paper.' Ebuka sits down, very slowly.

choices.label: Leave your share on the table. Walk out.
choices.receipt: You paid your share and walked out on her and her fiancé.

outcomes.text: You leave ₦20k under the salt. She follows you to the lift. You let the doors close.

choices.label: 'Ebuka. Buy me out. Like you're buying her.'
choices.receipt: You asked her fiancé to buy you out.

outcomes.text: Ebuka writes a cheque without blinking. ₦800k, 'consultancy'. She looks at you like you've sold her. You have.
'I don't pay for things I already own.' He says it to you. He's looking at her.

choices.label: Tell the whole terrace she's two-timing.
choices.receipt: You announced her engagement to the whole restaurant.

outcomes.text: Forty phones come out. Uncle's driver is in the car park by dessert. 'Heiress Gate' is trending by midnight.

choices.label: 'The 14th. You said family thing. This is the thing.'
choices.receipt: You reminded her of the 14th.

outcomes.text: She takes the ring off and puts it next to the salt. 'I was going to tell you on the 13th.' Ebuka excuses himself.

choices.label: Show her the lace-fitting photo from Admiralty Way.
choices.receipt: You showed her the photo of her ceremony fitting.

outcomes.text: She goes pale. 'You knew. And you stayed?' Ebuka looks at her very differently now.

choices.label: 'Computer Village, Ebuka. Your people?'
choices.receipt: You introduced yourself to her fiancé with your real pedigree.

outcomes.text: 'Oil.' He sounds bored saying it. She laughs. Not at you. At him. Something has decided itself.

beats.text: 8am, Admiralty Way. Six staff sitting on the boutique floor. A bank officer holding a padlock.
Please. Lend me ₦500k for payroll. Today. I'll pay you back Friday. I've never said please this much.
{tell}

collapsing.text: Outside, a tow truck backs up to her Range Rover. 'ASSET FINANCE' on the door.

choices.label: Lend the ₦500k. The staff need salary.
choices.broke_text: Your account is also on the floor.
choices.receipt: You lent her ₦500k for payroll.

outcomes.text: The staff cheer. She cries in the storeroom. You are a hero with no money.

choices.label: Pay one person's salary. ₦40k.
choices.receipt: You paid one staff member's salary.

outcomes.text: The cashier, Blessing, takes it and hugs you. Adaeze watches like she's learning something.

choices.label: Sit on the floor with them. Make a plan.
choices.receipt: You sat on the floor and built a rescue plan with her.

outcomes.text: Two hours. A clearance sale, a supplier deal, a loan restructure. She looks at you like a co-founder. Then like more.

choices.label: Offer to buy all her stock. At 10%.
choices.receipt: You bought her stock at 10% of value.

outcomes.text: You resell it on Instagram in four days. Profit: obscene. She finds out from her own customers.
Half of it is last season. You now own 300 sequinned blazers and nowhere to put them.

choices.label: Livestream the padlock. The Parlour loves a fall.
choices.receipt: You livestreamed her boutique being padlocked.

outcomes.text: 9,000 viewers. Her suppliers comment before she does. She looks at the camera, then at you, then never again.

choices.label: 'I'm not your payroll.' Walk out.
choices.receipt: You told her you're not her payroll and left.

outcomes.text: You step over the padlock chain. The tow truck honks goodbye. You don't look back.

choices.label: 'You still owe me from last time.'
choices.receipt: You told her she still owes you.

outcomes.text: She opens her purse. Car keys. 'Take the Range Rover. It isn't mine either.' The tow man laughs.

choices.label: 'I paid full price for a 70% off outfit.'
choices.receipt: You reminded her you paid full price for a sale outfit.

outcomes.text: She laughs, horribly, then properly. 'You did. You were my best customer that month.' The staff applaud you.

choices.label: 'Pay Sunday Okon first. Six kids.'
choices.receipt: You told her to pay the security man first.

outcomes.text: She pays Sunday from her own watch money. He salutes you both. 'Madam, this one is good.'

choices.label: 'Liquidity-challenged. You told me. I listened.'
choices.receipt: You told her you'd heard her liquidity joke.

outcomes.text: 'You caught that?' She sits on the floor. 'Then you know I've been drowning politely.' She lets you help.

beats.text: Her flat, midnight. Her eyes are red. Her uncle's voice note is still playing on the sofa.
A Computer Village family? Adaeze, end it. Or we end your shares.
I need you to know why I hid you. Then I need you to decide.
{tell}

tired.text: 'I hid you because Uncle buys them off. The last three took the money. All three.'

choices.label: 'Let him try. I'm not for sale.'
choices.receipt: You told her you're not for sale.

outcomes.text: She laughs and cries at once. 'That's all I needed. That's all I've ever needed.'

choices.label: Ask what Uncle is offering. Just to know.
choices.receipt: You asked how much her uncle was offering.

outcomes.text: '₦1 million,' she says quietly. 'The last one took ₦500k.' She watches your face like a stock price.

choices.label: 'So you were ashamed of me.'
choices.receipt: You accused her of being ashamed of you.

outcomes.text: She flinches. 'No. I was ashamed of THEM.' She opens the door and waits.

choices.label: 'I can't fight your whole family.' Leave.
choices.receipt: You left rather than fight her family.

outcomes.text: She doesn't stop you. One text: 'You were the realest thing. Be well.' You read it on the bridge.

choices.label: 'Computer Village, day one. Still proud.'
choices.receipt: You stood by your Computer Village roots.

outcomes.text: She forwards Uncle your exact words. Then switches her phone off. 'Let him chew on that.'

choices.label: Take her to the Ojuelegba amala spot. Now. Midnight.
choices.receipt: You took her for midnight amala at Ojuelegba.

outcomes.text: Plastic chairs, a generator, her heels in your hand. The Mama Put calls her 'my daughter'. She hasn't stopped smiling.

beats.text: Good morning. I called the palace in your village. They have never heard of Ichie you. Explain, or I explain to Adaeze.

choices.label: Confess to Uncle. Then to her, before he does.
choices.receipt: You confessed the fake title to her uncle and to her.

outcomes.text: She listens. 'You lied to impress people you don't even like. Okay. Don't do it again.'

tired.text: She laughs. 'Uncle called me first. I told him I knew. I didn't. Now I do. Thank you for not making me a liar.'

choices.label: 'It's a new title, sir. Very new.'
choices.receipt: You doubled down on the fake title.

outcomes.text: 'Hm.' He hangs up. You've bought one week, maybe two.
He forwards the call recording to her. And to the family WhatsApp. Forty-two members.

choices.label: Hang up. Block Uncle. Pray.
choices.receipt: You hung up on her uncle.

outcomes.text: He calls from three other numbers. Then he calls your mother. Your mother is on his side.

choices.label: [Runs] 'Uncle, how much to keep this between us?'
choices.receipt: You tried to bribe her uncle.

outcomes.text: He laughs for a long time. 'I like you. ₦0. But you'll call me Ichie from now on.'

beats.text: You went through my bag. My uncle has read my statements since I was nineteen. Not you too.

choices.label: 'I'm sorry. I was scared. Ask me anything back.'
choices.receipt: You apologised for going through her bag.

outcomes.text: She asks you three hard questions. You answer all three. She sits down next to you, not across.

tired.text: She asks three hard questions. You answer. 'Okay. I'll show you the notebook myself one day.'

choices.label: 'You were hiding something. Weren't you?'
choices.receipt: You told her she was hiding something.

outcomes.text: Long silence.

engaged.text: 'Yes.' She sits. 'There's a ring. It isn't my choice. I wanted to tell you properly.'

collapsing.text: 'Yes. Three default notices. I wanted to fix it before you saw. I'm so tired of fixing.'

tired.text: 'A notebook. About you. Happy?' She is not happy.

choices.label: 'I was looking for a charger.'
choices.receipt: You told her you were looking for a charger.

outcomes.text: She wants to believe you. She mostly does. She buys you a charger.
'In the zip pocket? Behind the letters?' She holds up her own charger.

beats.text: Good day. Uncle wants an updated report. For another ₦50k, I can keep 'very tall' in it.

choices.label: Pay him. Height is expensive.
choices.receipt: You paid the investigator a second time.

outcomes.text: 'Very tall' stays. He adds 'good teeth' as a free bonus.
He takes it, then texts: 'Same time next week?' You've got a subscription now.

choices.label: 'Write what you like, Lawal.'
choices.receipt: You refused to pay the investigator again.

outcomes.text: He writes 'Average height. Bribes poorly.' It's fair, honestly.

choices.label: Forward it to her. Own the first bribe.
choices.receipt: You told her you'd bribed her investigator.

outcomes.text: 'You bribed Lawal?' A pause. 'With ₦20k? He usually charges ₦100k.' She fires him anyway.

engaged.text: 'I didn't send Lawal. Uncle did. For... another family's file.' She goes quiet for the rest of the day.

collapsing.text: 'I stopped paying Lawal in March. He's freelancing you.' She laughs, then doesn't.

tired.text: She fires Lawal by voice note. Then calls you: 'I'm sorry I ever sent him. Bribing him was dumb, though.'

beats.text: Chidinma's email reached her first: 'Salary verification. Sources: LinkedIn, a payslip, your cousin's tweet.'
So. Your salary. Let's discuss the variance.

choices.label: 'I lied. I wanted to look like your world.'
choices.receipt: You admitted you'd inflated your salary.

outcomes.text: 'My world is exhausting. Don't move in.' She closes the email. Mostly forgiven.

tired.text: 'Modest was always the point, you mumu.' She kisses your forehead like a manager who's also in love.

collapsing.text: 'Oh.' She sounds disappointed for the wrong reason. She looks at the ceiling, doing maths.

choices.label: 'It's projected salary. Forward-looking.'
choices.receipt: You called your fake salary a projection.

outcomes.text: She snorts. 'Forward-looking. I'm stealing that for my investors.'
'Projections need assumptions. What's yours? That I'm stupid?'

choices.label: 'Your PA investigated me? Wow.'
choices.receipt: You complained that her PA had investigated you.

outcomes.text: 'Everyone gets investigated. You're the first one who lied.' Fair. Painful. Fair.

beats.text: Board ran late. I'm starving. You know what I actually want? Amala from that buka at Ojuelegba. Don't tell anyone. My mother thinks I eat salads.

choices.label: 'Ojuelegba amala. Your secret is safe. 🤐'
choices.receipt: You caught her secret amala craving.

outcomes.text: 'Don't make me laugh, I'm in a lift with my uncle.' Then a heart.

choices.label: 'Salad is self-care, babe.'
choices.receipt: You told her salad is self-care.

outcomes.text: 'You sound like my mother.' Read.

choices.label: Send your account number. 'For the amala.'
choices.receipt: You sent her your account number for amala.

outcomes.text: She sends ₦5k with the reference 'AMALA (UNBUDGETED)'.

beats.text: Can't do the 14th. Family thing in Enugu. Chidinma has blocked my whole Saturday. Don't ask, it's boring.

choices.label: 'The 14th, Enugu, family. Noted. 📌'
choices.receipt: You noted her 'family thing' on the 14th.

outcomes.text: 'You pin things.' A pause. 'I like that.' Another pause, longer.

choices.label: 'Enjoy! Bring me okpa.'
choices.receipt: You asked her to bring okpa back from Enugu.

outcomes.text: 'Okpa. Okay.' She sounds relieved you didn't ask anything else.

choices.label: 'Always family. When is it me?'
choices.receipt: You sulked about her family plans.

outcomes.text: 'Item 7: patience.' She's typing for a long time. Then she isn't.

beats.text: Sunday is the only day I don't wear heels. Funny, my security man is called Sunday. Sunday Okon. Six kids. Best man in Lagos. Anyway. Good morning.

choices.label: 'Greet Sunday Okon for me. Six kids is a whole team.'
choices.receipt: You remembered her security man, Sunday Okon.

outcomes.text: She plays your message to Sunday. He salutes the phone. She sends you the video.

choices.label: 'Send a no-heels picture.'
choices.receipt: You asked for a picture of her without heels.

outcomes.text: She sends a picture of her feet in Crocs. Pink Crocs. You'll die with this information.

choices.label: 'GM ☀️'
choices.receipt: You replied 'GM'.

outcomes.text: 'GM.' Two letters for a voice note. The minutes would not approve.

beats.text: Uncle Obiora hates two things: people who talk too much and people who don't eat. Just FYI. For no reason at all.

choices.label: 'Talk less, eat more. I was born for this.'
choices.receipt: You noted her uncle's two rules.

outcomes.text: 'Good. Don't make me regret the FYI.' She's smiling. You can tell from the punctuation.

choices.label: 'For no reason? 👀 Am I meeting Uncle?'
choices.receipt: You asked if you were meeting her uncle.

outcomes.text: 'No.' Then: 'Maybe.' Then: 'Don't be weird about it.'

choices.label: 'My uncle hates people who don't send money.'
choices.receipt: You hinted for money through your uncle.

outcomes.text: She sends ₦2k: 'For your uncle.' It's an insult and you both know it.

beats.text: I take minutes because my father did. He made Mummy sign them after every argument. I hate that I do it. Ignore me. It's late.

choices.label: 'You're not him. You can stop whenever. I'm listening.'
choices.receipt: You heard why she takes minutes.

outcomes.text: No reply for ten minutes. Then: 'Thank you.' No full stop. From her, that's a hug.

choices.label: 'Lol your dad was a whole board.'
choices.receipt: You laughed off her father story.

outcomes.text: 'Yes. Lol.' She goes offline.

choices.label: 'Sleep, CEO. Tomorrow is a meeting.'
choices.receipt: You told her to sleep.

outcomes.text: 'Yes sir/ma.' She sends a sleeping emoji and a calendar invite for breakfast.

beats.text: My accountant just called me 'liquidity-challenged'. To my face. That's a joke. Laugh. Anyway, dinner Thursday? You pick, I pay.

choices.label: 'Haha. Is everything okay, though? Actually okay?'
choices.receipt: You caught her 'liquidity' joke and asked if she was okay.

outcomes.text: 'Of course.' Then, a minute later: 'Mostly. Thursday. You pick.'

choices.label: 'Thursday. Ikoyi rooftop. You did say you pay.'
choices.receipt: You picked the expensive rooftop for her to pay.

outcomes.text: 'Of course.' The reply takes eleven minutes.

choices.receipt: You laughed at her liquidity joke.

outcomes.text: 'Exactly. Funny.' She sends a GIF of a man falling off a horse.
